entities.text:
High Court Of Jammu & Kashmir And Ladakh
 At Jammu
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
. The petitioners, by way of this petition, have sought a direction to the respondents to adhere to the provisions of the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013, and to refrain from taking forcible possession of the petitioners' land, measuring 14 Marlas (Khasra No. 1181), 01 Kanal 16 Marlas (Khasra No. 1182), 07 Kanals 07 Marlas (Khasra No. 1174), 05 Kanals 10 Marlas (Khasra No. 1160), and 08 Kanals 08 Marlas (Khasra No. 1166), situated at Mouza Lohma, Tehsil Dachhan, District Kishtwar, for the construction of a road from Ikhala Boundary to Lopara, Revenue Village Lohama, Tehsil Dachhan,
District Kishtwar.

entities.text:
Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition,
Rehabilitation and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 02. The petitioners have further sought a direction to the respondents to restrain them from taking possession of the aforesaid land without adhering to the provisions of the aforementioned Act and without paying compensation to the petitioner in lieu of the land as per the prevailing law.

03. The respondents have filed their objections wherein they have stated that the land of the petitioners is involved in the construction of a road namely Ikhalla Block Boundary Kishtwar to Bashir Ahmed Sheikh And vs Ut Of J&K And Others on 11 December, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/160808047/

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
, as per the report of the Tehsildar, Dachhan, issued vide letter No.
649/TD/Gen/2022-23, dated 08.12.2022 and that the same is being constructed in accordance with the law.

04. It is further stated that the road is aimed at connecting a significant portion of the population,
about 40,000 souls from Tehsil Dachhan as well as Marwah, who have been deprived of road connectivity since the dawn of independence and that the respondents have never interfered in the peaceful possession of the land belonging to the petitioners, and the possession of their land remains intact, as is evident from the site position of the same.

05. It is also stated that the right of respondent No. 3 in the said land would only arise after the proper placement of the indent before the Collector, Land Acquisition, by the head of the department, i.e., the Chief Engineer, PMGSY (J&K), Jammu, for the initiation of the project and after the proper acquisition of the land under the Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Act, 2013.

entities.text: Right to Fair Compensation and Transparency in Land Acquisition, Rehabilitation, and Resettlement Act, 2013
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The acquisition papers for the land are currently in their final stages with the Collector, Land Acquisition (SDM Marwah).

06. It is specifically stated in the objections that that the land of the petitioners will be acquired only in accordance with the law and upon payment of compensation, as the road project is of great importance.

07. Learned counsel for the petitioners has relied upon the order passed by this Court on 30.06.21022 in WP(C) No. 174/2021, titled 'Shabir Ahmad Yatoo vs. UT of J&K and others' and seeks disposal of the instant writ petition on the same analogy.

entities.text: Shabir Ahmad Yatoo vs. UT of J&K and others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 08. In view of the submission made by the learned counsel for the petitioners, this petition is disposed of with a direction to the respondents to assess and determine the compensation for the aforesaid land payable to the petitioners at the prevailing stamp duty rate in the area, within a period of six weeks and after assessing the same, shall release the amount of compensation in favour of the petitioners within a period of two weeks thereafter.

(Sindhu Sharma) Judge Jammu:
